articles.title: NBI tapped to probe woman’s death after plastic surgery
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) was tapped to look into the death of a woman who supposedly died after undergoing plastic surgery procedures performed by a celebrity…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) was tapped to look into the death of a woman who supposedly died after undergoing plastic surgery procedures performed by a celebrity plastic surgeon in San Juan City.

The woman’s son, Ronn Tristan Perez, who is a Filipino-American reality television star based in the United States, arrived at the NBI’s Homicide Division on Thursday to seek the investigation into the death of his mother.
In an interview with reporters, Perez said his mother underwent four cosmetic procedures — such as liposuction, Brazilian butt lift, tummy tuck, and body tite for arms — on March 2.
He said these procedures cost P570,000 and were performed by the celebrity surgeon for seven hours.

“Just a quick Google search of it, those are the most dangerous things that you can perform. So you should do due diligence before you even do it. And then even extra care while you’re doing it. And extra care afterwards. That’s like common knowledge,” Perez said.
“And so I’m hoping that all of that was taken into consideration. That people weren’t just taking her money, preying on her insecurities about her looks and making a quick buck off of her,” he added.
According to Perez, his mother started becoming pale after undergoing the four plastic surgery procedures at the celebrity surgeon’s clinic.
“I FaceTime her, and she’s pale, she’s missing a tooth. I said, ‘What’s happening, Mom?’ Me and my brother were both worried,” Perez said.
“Next thing I know, 3 a.m., a couple of days later, I get a phone call from my uncle and my dad, and it was my mom dead.”
Perez claimed he asked the clinic for his mother’s medical records but did not receive all of the documents he wanted to see.

“I’m not accusing anyone of anything. I need more than that. I need documents, papers, expertise that what was done here is everything that was supposed to be done. No stones left unturned,” said Perez.
The NBI is currently looking into the matter. /das

articles.title: TV presenter v secret son: the succession dispute engulfing a Ugandan kingdom
articles.summary:
Family of late King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV reveal son’s existence as they reject committee’s choice of cousin as new monarch

A traditional Ugandan kingdom has become engulfed in…
articles.byline: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies

blocks.text: A traditional Ugandan kingdom has become engulfed in a bitter succession dispute after the family of a king who recently died rejected the selection of a television news anchor as his successor.

King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, who became the world’s youngest reigning monarch when he took the throne in the kingdom of Tooro in 1995 at the age of three, died on 27 August in the US, where he was receiving cancer treatment.

blocks.caption: King Oyo Nyimba, aged 13, sits between his mother Best Kemigisha and an unidentified adviser during celebrations marking his first decade in power in Fort Portal, Uganda. Photograph: Reuters

blocks.text: On Wednesday, the royal clan’s succession committee announced it had chosen Oyo’s cousin Prince Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, a news anchor and editor at the public broadcaster UBC, as crown prince.

However, at a press conference held later the same day, Oyo’s sister, Princess Ruth Nsemere Komuntale, said that according to her brother’s will, a son whose existence had not been publicly known until his death should succeed him.

blocks.caption: Princess Ruth Komuntale waiting to receive the body of her brother, the late King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, at Entebbe International airport last week. Photograph: Hajarah Nalwadda/Getty Images

blocks.text: The kingdom’s ‌spokesperson shared a section of the document, which says: “I hereby declare and direct that if, at the date of my death, I am survived by a son lawfully recognised as my biological son, I appoint him as my heir to the throne of the kingdom of Tooro.”

In a statement on Thursday, Oyo’s mother, Queen Mother Best Kemigisa Akiiki, denounced a “self-appointed group of clan members” who had selected a new king despite having had the will read to them hours earlier.

blocks.caption: A portrait of the late king on the red carpet at Entebbe International airport. Photograph: Hajarah Nalwadda/Getty Images

blocks.text: Oyo was unmarried and was not known to have any children. The Tooro kingdom’s prime minister, Calvin Armstrong Rwomiire Akiiki, revealed the existence of a son in a social media post on 27 August when announcing Oyo’s death.
“His majesty leaves behind a prince as his heir, whose identity will be formally revealed at the appropriate time, in accordance with the traditions and customs of Tooro kingdom,” he said.

The Tooro king is selected by a succession committee appointed by the royal clan. A committee member told the local NTV station that a royal child must be officially introduced to elders in order to be considered for leadership.

blocks.caption: Queen Mother Best Kemigisa Akiiki waiting to receive the body of her son at Entebbe International airport. Photograph: Hajarah Nalwadda/Getty Images

blocks.text: Andrew Mwenda, ⁠a prominent Ugandan journalist and relative of the royal family, wrote on X on Thursday that Oyo’s ​family had not been able to produce a photo ​of the purported son, and declined to disclose ​details about the family of the boy’s mother. He added that, in Tooro, a king’s son could only succeed ​him if he were born to ‌a queen officially married ​to the king.

The prime minister ​called for restraint on Thursday. “There will be time to examine the will, to hear those advancing a different position, and to consider our customs, the applicable law and the proper institutions through which succession should be determined,” he said in a social media post.
“That process should take place calmly and credibly, not through competing announcements, confrontation, or attempts to establish facts on the ground while our king still awaits burial.”

blocks.caption: Uganda’s president, Yoweri Museveni, lays a wreath on the casket of the king at Entebbe International airport. Photograph: Hajarah Nalwadda/Getty Images

blocks.text: Edward, a popular TV news presenter, is the son of Prince Christopher Paul Kijanangoma and a grandson of the former king George David Rukidi III.
Oyo, who was crowned after his father’s death, will be buried on Saturday at the Karambi royal tombs in the kingdom’s capital of Fort Portal in western Uganda.

Uganda has several ancient kingdoms that lack formal sovereignty, but whose leaders are revered as symbols of tradition and wield vast social influence. Tooro is one of five that are recognised by the government. Their monarchs have no political authority and are legally barred from engaging in partisan politics.
In 1967 Uganda’s then president, Milton Obote, abolished the kingdoms, saying he wanted to unify the country. They were restored by the current president, Yoweri Museveni, in 1993.

blocks.caption: The casket of the late king arrives at Entebbe International airport. Photograph: Hajarah Nalwadda/Getty Images

blocks.text: The Tooro are the latest African royal family to become mired in a succession dispute. King Misuzulu Sinqobile kaZwelithini, the reigning king of the Zulu people in South Africa, waited 15 months for his coronation after the death of his father because of a bitter feud involving accusations of forgery and poisoning.
Reuters and the Associated Press contributed reporting

articles.title: AJ Edu’s versatility draws praise from Gunma teammates, coach
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines—AJ Edu is slowly making his mark with the Gunma Crane Thunders, and former NBA journeyman Stanley Johnson has taken notice. Johnson is still finding his way with Gunma after…

blocks.text: Gunma Crane Thunders Filipino AJ Edu during the Japan B.League Manila preseason games. –B.LEAGUE PHOTO
MANILA, Philippines—AJ Edu is slowly making his mark with the Gunma Crane Thunders, and former NBA journeyman Stanley Johnson has taken notice.
Johnson is still finding his way with Gunma after leaving Nagasaki Velca, but he already likes what Edu brings to the Crane Thunders.

“He adds a lot of size to our lineup. He has his rebounding, versatility and finishing,” Johnson said after Gunma’s 101-91 overtime win over Levanga Hokkaido at Mall of Asia Arena on Thursday. “He’s good at screening angles, especially against teams who love to switch on us.”
Edu showed his impact in the win with a near double-double of nine points and nine rebounds.
He also helped make the job easier for Johnson, who won a title with Velca last season, as the forward finished with 17 points.
Gunma coach Kyle Milling also praised Edu, saying the Gilas Pilipinas big man brings more than just his physicality.
According to Milling, Edu’s court vision is not to be underestimated as well.
“Last night, he had four assists and at one point last season, he had six assists,” said the coach. “He’s a great passer as well.”

articles.title: Explainer: Why are the Sierra Madre and nature-based solutions important vs floods?
articles.summary: Rising up to 6,283 feet and with a length of 540 kilometers, the Sierra Madre Mountain Range serves as the backbone of Luzon Island and one of the most important land formations in the Philippines.

blocks.text: Rising up to 6,283 feet and with a length of 540 kilometers, the Sierra Madre Mountain Range serves as the backbone of Luzon Island and one of the most important land formations in the Philippines.
GMA News’ Jasmine Gabriel-Galban said the Sierra Madre has 40 percent of the country’s forest cover which serves as the primary defense of many provinces against seasonal typhoons.

But based on a study by the Haribon Foundation, the Sierra Madre loses 9,000 hectares of forest cover annually due to illegal logging and timber poaching, excessive mining, quarrying and kaingin (a traditional method of agriculture where farmers clear forest or woodland by cutting down and burning trees and vegetation to plant crops).
Add to these are developmental projects and the construction of structures on the mountain range itself.
From 2003 to 2020, a total of 130,000 hectares of forest cover has been lost in the Sierra Madre.

Experts have warned that if this continues, the Sierra Madre will gradually weaken in its capacity to act as Luzon’s protective wall and that the mountains that defend many areas would themselves trigger many calamities.
According to urban planner Paolo Alcazaren, a renowned architect, many communities in the Philippines are flood-prone since these are located downstream of rivers or in coastal lowlands.
Similar to a batya or washing basin, water will flow to the lowest point and settle in the middle.

“Majority of the 1,500 towns and cities in the Philippines are at the bottom of the slope from each of the islands. So there are uplands where the rain falls, ‘yung tubig baha will fall from that. But because we are deforested more than 90% of the original forest cover is gone. All of that water is going down to the 16 major river basins and river systems in the Philippines. And at the bottom of all of these are most of our towns and cities,” he said.

As an example, Metro Manila is situated on a low-lying floodplain that is bordered on two sides by the Manila Bay and Laguna de Bay that are both connected by the Pasig River. To the north of the Laguna de Bay is the Sierra Madre Mountain Range. During heavy rains, water flows from the Sierra Madre downwards via river systems connected to the Laguna de Bay. When the Laguna de Bay’s water level rises simultaneously with high tide in the Manila Bay, the accumulated water has nowhere else to go except to the roads of Metro Manila.
Alcazaren said no matter how many flood control projects are undertaken, if there are no solutions for the floods coming from upstream or higher elevations, the problem will just continue.

“Reliance on gray infrastructure is not the ultimate solution, which really needs to happen at the upper elevations. First for reforestation; second to detain the rain water before it gets down via dams, via detention ponds. To use bioengineering or nature-based solutions, the rivers and waterways that we have,” the architect said.
Nature-based solutions also include open parks and green spaces that will absorb the water that would help prevent floods but a hurdle to their implementation is a lack of sufficient laws.

“In other progressive cities around the world, their nature-based flood mitigation, and some modern management, is based on a network of parks and open spaces. Unfortunately, in our towns and cities, we have not built any major park, much less a park system in the last 50, 60, 70 years,” Alcazaren observed.
There is also a lack of coordination and cooperation between public officials.

“Stormwaters do not recognize political boundaries, yet we seek to address these problems. ‘Oh, I’m the mayor of this town or city and I will solve the problems of flooding within our city.’, [It] just doesn’t work that way,” he said.

“What is lacking is coordination and collaboration, and venues for such collaboration and cooperation are non-existent because of apparent lack of admission of accountability and responsibility across the board in all our institutions,” Alcazaren pointed out.

In August 2026, Malacanang announced the placing of nature-based flooding solutions in different parts of Metro Manila. Among these are the building of detention basins in areas of higher elevations, river floodplains and inland wetlands.
The Protected Area Management Board is also pushing for steps that would broaden the conservation and management of protected areas in the Sierra Madre.

In Congress, there is a proposal to create the Sierra Madre Mountain Range Authority and a 10-year ban on logging, mining and infrastructure projects and any type of development within the mountain range.
These measures aim to restore 50,000 hectares of protected land and to secure ancestral domains of the Dumagat-Remontado and Agta communities.

Experts have proposed many solutions to counter flooding and they say it is now the time for the government to listen to what they have to say in order to lift the country from the floods that are drowning Filipinos into an ordeal. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: MPs on both sides urge Commons not to take ‘extraordinary risk’ of forcing through assisted dying bill
articles.summary: Labour MPs Gareth Snell and Meg Hillier say Lords must be allowed to fulfil duty in scrutinising bill on serious public issue

blocks.text: MPs who voted for and against assisted dying have urged their respective sides not to take the “extraordinary risk” of forcing through the bill using an obscure parliamentary procedure if it continues to be blocked by the Lords.
Two Labour MPs have written a warning letter to colleagues in the crucial hours before the next vote on Friday: Gareth Snell, who voted in favour of the bill, and Meg Hillier, who voted against.

They said MPs were being presented with a “this or nothing” ultimatum and that invoking the Parliament Act to override the Lords would lead to “a constitutional showdown” with far-reaching consequences.
“Our primacy as the elected house is more than a right to enforce our will; it is a responsibility to exercise our power with the greatest of care,” Snell and Hillier wrote.

But in a countering letter, a Labour MP and a Conservative MP argued that the Parliament Act would only be used as a last resort, if the Lords sought to block the stated will of the Commons, as happened with the last version, when it was talked out by a handful of peers who tabled a huge number of amendments.

Sarah Champion and Kit Malthouse, both of whom backed the last bill, said they were happy for the Lords to suggest improvements to the new version, but that the Parliament Act was necessary to ensure “the unelected Lords cannot repeatedly block legislation passed by the elected house”.

The private member’s bill, originally sponsored by Kim Leadbeater, has been revived by another Labour MP Lauren Edwards. It had passed last year by a majority of 23 in the Commons. Supportive MPs and peers say they can use the 1911 Parliament Act to override the Lords and pass the bill should it be voted through again by the Commons.

But some MPs have expressed uneasiness at the use of the act to bypass the House of Lords on such a serious issue. The bill would allow adults with a terminal illness with less than six months to live to end their lives, after the approval of a panel of experts.
after newsletter promotion

Since 1949, when it was revised, the Parliament Act has been used to enact just a handful of laws that have not had the consent of the Lords, including decriminalising homosexuality and banning foxhunting.

After a session of parliament ends, a bill must be reintroduced and passed again in the new session to trigger the act’s override mechanism. It must be exactly the same version of the bill as previously passed by the Commons.

In their letter to MPs, Snell and Hillier said the determination of the bill’s backers to use the Parliament Act meant there would be no possibility of “practical or worthwhile amendments” being added, despite concerns from hospices, medical professionals, legal bodies and others.

“This is an extraordinary risk for us to take,” they wrote. “We know that the colleagues who have brought the bill forward did so in good faith. They have sought to start a conversation many feel is overdue about an issue that is manifestly of interest to the public.

“However, the consequences of what may happen this week go much further. We both want the House of Lords to fulfil its duties, but bringing back an identical bill devoid of the previously agreed amendments sets up a constitutional showdown through an issue which deserves much more thoughtful consideration.”

In their letter, Champion and Malthouse said that Edwards and other bill sponsors had tabled some amendments to improve the original bill, and that they were open to these being debated and voted on by peers.

In a separate statement, Edwards said the measure was only having to be tabled and debated again “because a small number of peers chose to prevent any votes taking place on the bill earlier this year and so blocked its passage. That was undemocratic and brought one of the most significant national conversations we have had as legislators to an abrupt halt.
“There is a real human cost to the delay in passing this legislation and correcting the injustices and cruelty of the current law.”

articles.title: African Parks: When conservation becomes a question of power
articles.summary: African Parks is dedicated to protecting wildlife on the continent across some vast areas. But the organization faces allegations of human rights abuses by rangers. Now, Prince Harry is stepping down…

image.caption: Around 2,800 elephants live in Pendjari in Benin, one of 24 national parks managed by "African Parks" in on the continentImage: Katrin Gänsler/DW

blocks.text: Prince Harry has long been a supporter of African wildlife and nature. When the British royal first became involved with African Parks in 2016, he served as a prominent figure supporting awareness on elephant conservation.
Later, the son of King Charles III became president of the organization before joining its board in 2023.
But reports indicate that in just a few weeks' time, he will step down from his position at African Parks. The NGO claims that the move is merely part of a reshuffling of its board.

But Dutch journalist and author Olivier van Beemen, who has extensively investigated the South Africa-based wildlife conservation group, believes the association between Harry and African Parks has increasingly become a burden — for both sides.

blocks.caption: Prince Harry served as President of African Parks from 2017 to 2023, before joining the Board of Directors.Image: Rwanda Presidency/AA/picture alliance

blocks.text: Prince harming

Harry's role was to mainly open doors for African Parks, van Beemen says. His fame attracted media attention and helped the NGO gain access to potential donors. But his notorious falling-out with his family increasingly failed to improve the organization's coffers and image.
At the same time, allegations of human rights abuses at African Parks made the prince's association with the organization increasingly problematic.

"I think they now see each other more as a liability," van Beemen told DW, stressing that the full story reaches far beyond a junior member of the royal family simply stepping down from a ribbon-cutting role.
An NGO with state-like powers
According to its own figures, African Parks manages 24 protected areas in 13 African countries, covering more than 20 million hectares. By 2030, the organization aims to manage as many as 30 parks.
Its business model is known as delegated management: African governments hand over the long-term management of protected areas to the group.
The land formally remains state-owned. But the organization takes on wide-ranging responsibilities, including conservation, infrastructure, tourism and anti-poaching operations.

For African governments, this model offers a major advantage: African Parks brings international funding, expertise and personnel to protected areas that many states would otherwise struggle to manage on their own.

In order to achieve its objectives on the ground, African Parks employs a host of armed rangers across the continent, who are allowed to use indelicate methods if and when needed; in some cases, its influence even extends to managing border controls.

"They take over the state's monopoly on the use of force within the park," says van Beemen, adding that some critics of the NGO have gone as far as describing African Parks as a "state within a state."
It is in this context that mounting allegations of human rights abuses have been recorded in recent years, with conservation efforts repeatedly coming into conflict with local communities.
The shadow of the Baka case
The worst allegations of rights abuses relate to Odzala-Kokoua National Park in the Republic of Congo, which emerged in 2023.
Members of the indigenous Baka community reported violence, torture and sexual abuse at the hands of African Parks' rangers.

The NGO subsequently commissioned the London-based firm Omnia Strategy to investigate the allegations, resulting in African Parks acknowledging certain instances of human rights abuses two years later — though the full investigation report was never made public.

According to van Beemen, the report was not even shown to the government of the Republic of Congo, despite African Parks operating there under an agreement with the government. To this day, it remains unclear what exactly happened in Odzala-Kokoua, and how many people were affected.
African Parks has promised reforms, merely highlighting alleged failures in its own systems and processes in the past but has remained intransparent about the entire scandal, says van Beemen.

blocks.caption: Dutch journalist Olivier van Beemen visited numerous wildlife reserves run by African Parks, including the Majete Wildlife Reserve in MalawiImage: privat

blocks.text: Division over findings in Dutch book
The Dutch journalist has meanwhile published a book on the whole affair, titled "Beasts and Men." The volume won several awards in the Netherlands, and has attracted international attention.

But African Parks fundamentally rejects van Beemen's portrayal of the organization, saying his book contains "hundreds of factual inaccuracies" as well as "a similar number of deeply misleading statements."
Regarding the human rights allegations, African Parks says some of the cases described by van Beemen had occurred outside the NGOs control.

At the same time, it stressed in a statement that it has a zero-tolerance policy toward abuse, and that there is training in place on human rights training as well as a detailed complaints mechanisms.

blocks.caption: Armed rangers patrol areas managed by African Parks, including some national bordersImage: DW

blocks.text: But as part of his research, van Beemen also spoke to several former rangers and people affected by conservation operations in several African countries, where he says he repeatedly encountered a fundamental problem perpetuated by African Parks: the loose definition of what constitutes poaching.

According to the accounts he collected, the NGO also treats some locals who hunt animals for their own consumption as poachers, rather than using the terms exclusive to describe professional poachers who kill rhinos or elephants for international criminal networks.

Van Beemen said that during his research in Zambia, former rangers told him about the brutal treatment the people taken into custody on such grounds can face: "This can involve beatings. It can involve very serious torture," he told DW.
Hiding behind a colonial mindset?

The history of African Parks is also controversial. The organization was founded by Dutch businessman Paul Fentener van Vlissingen, who — according to van Beemen — refused to accept the international economic sanctions against the South African apartheid system during the 1980s.

A former close associate of the founde told the Dutch journalist that at the top echolons of the organization, Africans were allegedly considered incapable of protecting their own natural resources because they lacked the money and management skills to do so.

blocks.caption: Anti-poaching initiatives are among the many responsibilities covered by the NGOImage: Mujahid Safodien/AFP

blocks.text: In its early years, African Parks was headquartered in the Netherlands where according to van Beemen, employees would routinely look at maps of Africa and plan where the organization could take over additional parks.
"For me, it was very difficult not to think of the colonialists of earlier centuries looking at the same maps and searching for opportunities for colonial expansion," van Beemen told Dw.
African Parks meanwhile also rejects this characterization, pointing out at the relevant contracts it has signed with African governments.
Conservation and accountability

The scandal also hits closer to Europe not only because of Prince Harry's departure from the NGO but also due to the fact that European and German funding also goes to projects involving African Parks.
The organization stresses that cooperations with local communities is at the heart of its work:
It says that there are people living in 64% of the areas it manages, while legal access to resources is allowed in 90% of the parks. Only four of the 23 parks are fully fenced, it added.
But without sufficient scrutiny and accountability, there is no way of verifying the details behind those claims, as the image of the NGO continues to tank.

articles.title: Orthodox church sends medieval prince’s remains to Russian troops in Ukraine
articles.summary: Part of Dmitry Donskoy’s right hand sent to ‘spiritually strengthen’ soldiers

blocks.text: The Russian Orthodox church has sent a fragment of a medieval warrior prince’s remains to troops fighting in Ukraine, saying the relic would “spiritually strengthen” soldiers and help them achieve victory.

A reliquary containing part of the right hand of Dmitry Donskoy, the 14th-century prince revered in Russia for his victory over the Mongolian Golden Horde in 1380, has been taken to Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and is now being transported along the frontline.

The Russian Orthodox church said in a statement: “The holy commander is going to where the fate of the fatherland is being decided today, so that he may invisibly take his place in the same battle ranks as our defenders.”

The relic was first brought on Tuesday to the Saur-Mogila war memorial in the Russian-occupied Donetsk region of Ukraine, where senior Orthodox clergy held a prayer service alongside representatives of the Russian military.
The Russian-installed Metropolitan Vladimir of Donetsk and Mariupol said its presence would help soldiers and civilians “mobilise their strength” and secure victory over the enemy.

The relic’s journey is the latest example of the Russian Orthodox church’s rabid embrace of the Kremlin’s war in Ukraine, which Patriarch Kirill, its leader, has repeatedly portrayed in religious terms.

Since Vladimir Putin launched the full-scale invasion in February 2022, the church hierarchy has become deeply embedded in the Russian war effort. Priests have been sent to military units and occupied territories; while churches across Russia have been instructed to recite prayers asking God to grant victory.
Donskoy’s relics were first formally uncovered only last month during restoration work at the Cathedral of the Archangel inside the Kremlin, where generations of Russian princes and tsars are buried.
Putin, who has grown increasingly close to the Russian Orthodox church over his more than two decades in power, personally attended the ceremony marking the unearthing.

Critics have accused the church of breaking with religious protocol by opening Donskoy’s centuries-old tomb. The location of the prince’s burial had long been known, but the church had previously made no attempt to exhume his remains after he was canonised in 1988.

Alexander Zanemonets, an Orthodox priest and historian based outside Russia, said the decision to uncover the relics almost four decades after Donskoy’s canonisation appeared driven by the demands of wartime patriotism.

He wrote in a piece for the Carnegie thinktank: “By the fifth year of war, the church leadership in Moscow began to wonder what else it could do to show its support for what Russia terms its ‘special military operation’.”

Zanemonets said the portrayal of Donskoy as a defender of the homeland fitted neatly with the Kremlin’s insistence that Russia was defending itself rather than conducting a war of aggression against its neighbour.
Earlier this year, relics of Alexander Nevsky, another medieval prince and military hero revered by the Russian Orthodox church, were also sent to the front.

articles.title: BJMP ready to transfer Romualdez to Payatas jail once order issued
articles.summary: The Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) continues to secure the hospital where former Speaker Martin Romualdez is confined.

blocks.text: Published September 10, 2026 11:11pm
The Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) continues to secure the hospital where former Speaker Martin Romualdez is confined.
In a "24 Oras" report from Mariz Umali on Thursday, the Sandiganbayan Third Division has ordered the transfer of custody of Romualdez to the BJMP.

“Nakalagay naman po yun doon na dadalhin siya sa kulungan sa BJMP Quezon City Jail sa Payatas, Quezon City…Nakahanda lang po ang BJMP in any eventuality,” said BJMP spokesperson Jayrex Joseph Bustinera. (It is said there that he will be taken to the BJMP Quezon City Jail in Payatas, Quezon City… the BJMP is ready for any eventuality.)
Romualdez is charged with plunder over the P7.4 billion alleged flood control kickbacks.
The BJMP said that Romualdez will not receive any special treatment, nor will he be confined in a solo cell.

“Meron pong definitely may makakasama po siya doon… kung ano meron doon sa flood control accused, pati yung other high-profile PDL (persons deprived of liberty) natin, same, pare-pareho lang po ang design ng selda doon,” Bustinera said.
(Definitely he will be with someone there… what happens with the other flood control accused and other high-profile PDLs, it is the same, the cells are all designed the same.)
The BJMP also said that they have adequate medical facilities. There are also in-house medical doctors and nurses who are available around the clock.
Romualdez’s doctors have yet to clear him for travel.

“The patient is medically unfit to travel outside the hospital as of now to physically appear for the Sandiganbayan. Yun po ang nilabas today. Yun ang inilabas nilang certification (That was what was released today. That was what was on the certification),” said Philippine National Police spokesperson Police Colonel Allan Rae Co said.
The former speaker will remain in the hospital while the court hears his petition for hospital confinement.
No one could visit Romualdez other than his immediate family, legal counsel, and his doctors. Once he is given medical clearance, however, he will be transported to the Quezon CIty Jail.
The hospital said that Romualdez’s doctors will not release a medical bulletin for Thursday night.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Dwight Ramos feels Filipino crowd’s love wherever he plays
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines—Dwight Ramos once again felt the frenzy of the Filipino crowd during the Japan B.League Manila Games. By now, though, the situation is hardly a surprise. READ: Dwight Ramos ‘big…

blocks.text: Levanga Hokkaido’s Dwight Ramos during the Japan B.League Manila preseason games. –B.LEAGUE PHOTO
MANILA, Philippines—Dwight Ramos once again felt the frenzy of the Filipino crowd during the Japan B.League Manila Games.
By now, though, the situation is hardly a surprise.
After playing for Gilas Pilipinas around the world, Ramos said playing at home–even for a Japanese club–felt much the same.

“I play in Japan and there’s a lot of Filipinos there. I played in the Middle East, and there’s also a lot of Filipinos there. I play here and the gym’s packed,” he said. “I can’t even tell the difference. It’s the same everywhere I go.”
“No matter where I go, I get the same crowd where I play. I really appreciate it and I’m really grateful for it.”

blocks.caption: Fans at Mall of Asia Arena during the Japan B.League Manila preseason games.

blocks.text: Fans at Mall of Asia Arena during the Japan B.League Manila preseason games. –B.LEAGUE PHOTO
The rowdy home crowd fueled Ramos to drop 17 points, four assists and three rebounds.
His Levanga Hokkaido, however, fell to the Gunma Crane Thunders for the second straight night, this time a 101-91 loss in overtime Thursday at Mall of Asia Arena.
On the other side, AJ Edu nearly tallied a double-double with nine points and nine rebounds.
Like Ramos, Edu was ecstatic to feel the home crowd again, but he was happier to see his Gunma teammates experience the Filipino fans’ passion.

“It’s great that they also experienced how Filipino fans are,” said Edu. “This isn’t quite like Gilas but I always talk about their passion so I’m grateful that my team got to experience that firsthand.”

articles.title: ‘I don’t want to be here’: Andrew Hastie was a reluctant but ‘straightforward’ witness in the Ben Roberts-Smith defamation case
articles.summary:
The Liberal MP and former SAS soldier is under attack from One Nation after complying with a subpoena to give evidence in the failed 2022 civil case

  • Get our

blocks.text: “I don’t dislike Mr Roberts-Smith at all. I pity Mr Roberts-Smith. I pity this whole process. I don’t want to be here.”

Andrew Hastie was a reluctant witness in the Ben Roberts-Smith defamation case. Hastie appeared only under force of subpoena in 2022: compelled to attend court, obliged to swear an oath, and to tell “the whole truth and nothing but the truth”.

His was an unhappy (of many) visit to the witness box. But it brought with it an additional scrutiny: he was, at the time of the case, not only a member of parliament, but the assistant minister for defence. Of the dozens of former SAS soldiers compelled to give evidence to the defamation case – many resentfully – Hastie was the only one named and photographed, the only one not afforded the protection of being a “sensitive witness”.

In his judgment, Justice Anthony Besanko was approbative: “Mr Hastie was an honest and straightforward witness.” Three times, in fact, he characterised the former officer, now MP, as “straightforward” in his testimony.
Of Hastie’s former comrade who brought the defamation case – Victoria Cross recipient Ben Roberts-Smith – Besanko was equally forthright, but less complimentary.
“[Roberts-Smith] was not an honest and reliable witness.
“In each case, [his] motive for the lie is the realisation of guilt and a fear of the truth.”

Now, for his testimony, Hastie has been referred to as a “gutless maggot” and a “traitor” in a cartoon posted online by Pauline Hanson’s One Nation party. Hanson, personally, said she would prefer to call Hastie a “wanker”.
‘Blooding’

Membership of “the regiment” – the SAS – is famously clandestine. Roberts-Smith and Hastie are perhaps its best-known former members. The pair’s service, while contemporaneous, was not tightly aligned. They are not close.

Hastie, an officer, has written he remembers his first encounter with Roberts-Smith – the corporal ordering officer candidates into push-ups in a dead-of-night training exercise. He told the federal court there was a “widespread view” across the SAS that Roberts-Smith was a bully.

Before the federal court, Hastie was asked to testify as to his recollection of an operation on a compound in a village known as Syachow in October 2012. It was his only operation in Afghanistan alongside Roberts-Smith.
It was alleged before the federal court that on that mission Roberts-Smith ordered a subordinate soldier – known as Person 66 – to execute an unarmed prisoner in a so-called “blooding” incident.
Hastie did not shy away from recounting details of the event in his testimony.
Person 66, too, was subpoenaed to appear in court. He refused to answer a question about whether he’d been on operation in Afghanistan with Roberts-Smith as his patrol commander.
“Person 66 objected to giving an answer to that question on the ground that it may tend to prove that he had committed the offence of the war crime of murder,” Besanko wrote in his judgment.
On those grounds, Besanko could not find the allegation proved.
Asked directly whether he ordered Person 66 to kill an unarmed prisoner, Roberts-Smith told the court: “I did not.”
after newsletter promotion
Hastie told the court he once held Robert-Smith in “very high regard”.
“I am no longer proud of Mr Roberts-Smith.”
‘Shoot him’
The alleged incident at Syahchow is one of the five war crimes murders with which Roberts-Smith has since been criminally charged.

The statement of facts before the court reads that two PUCs – Persons Under Control – were hors de combat after an SAS raid on a compound. The two prisoners were handcuffed and blindfolded at the cessation of the raid.

“Roberts-Smith cut the handcuffs from PUC 1 who was in front of Person 66, removed PUC 1’s blindfold and pushed him to the ground. PUC 1 fell backwards and put his hand in front of his face with his palms facing outwards. Roberts-Smith said ‘shoot him’.
“Person 66 believed this to be an order from Roberts-Smith. Person 66 was two metres away from PUC 1. Person 66 paused for a moment and then shot PUC 1 two to three times in the chest, killing him.”
The statement of facts states: “Person 66 has admitted their role in this incident.”
Roberts-Smith’s case is now before the courts. He has consistently and vigorously denied the allegations against him.

“For the past 10 years, my family and I have been subject to a campaign to convince Australians that I’ve acted improperly in my service in Afghanistan,” Roberts-Smith said in a statement after he was charged.
“As I’ve always maintained, I categorically deny all of these allegations, and while I would’ve preferred these charges not be brought, I will be taking the opportunity to finally clear my name.
“I have never run from a fight in my life. I will never give up, and I will always be in the fight.”

articles.title: Woolworths increased prices of at least four ‘family staples’ during ‘Price Freeze’ promotion
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Analysis shows cost of chicken fillets, potatoes and donuts rose during supermarket giant’s three-month promotion

  • Get our

blocks.text: Woolworths raised prices for popular items – including a 33% mark up on chicken fillets – within days of promising to freeze prices on 300 “family staples” for three months to help customers with the cost of living.

Pricing data, compiled by comparison website CW Scanner and provided to Guardian Australia, shows the supermarket chain increasing the prices of at least four key products after starting the three-month “Price Freeze” promotion on 1 May.

The supermarket nearly doubled the price of a 420g can of Woolworths “Mexican Style 3 Bean Mix” during the promotional period – from 60c to $1 on 17 June – the data shows. Woolworths dropped the price back to 60c on 17 August.

Woolworths declined to comment on the analysis. But it is understood that it justified the increases during the “Price Freeze” because it regarded the previous prices as promotional prices, rather than the “standard shelf price” for each product.

When the price freeze was announced, the Woolworths chief executive officer, Amanda Bardwell, said the supermarket wanted to help customers who were concerned about how inflation driven by the war on Iran was affecting household budgets.

“That’s why, for the next three months, we’re freezing the shelf price on 300 staples that families rely on most, like eggs, chicken breast fillets, pasta, beef sausages and nappies,” Bardwell said in a press release on 30 April.

“It’s our promise that the shelf price you see on these items today is the most you’ll pay for the next three months. We’ll invest to absorb any extra costs that are agreed with suppliers on these products to make that happen.”

Prof Jana Bowden, a marketing expert and chair of ethics at Macquarie University’s business school, said raising prices after claiming they had been fixed was “akin to not delivering on the everyday consumer’s interpretation of a ‘price freeze’ promise”.
“How is the consumer expected to know what the start prices were before the campaign or even after the campaign started?” Bowden said.
“No consumer walks into a supermarket with the insights of how the prices for the hundreds of products that they buy vary over a day, week, month or year – nor should they have to.”
The analysis comes at a time of high scrutiny of the pricing tactics used by Woolworths – and rival Coles – after landmark court cases involving both companies.

Woolworths is awaiting the verdict in the federal court case brought against it by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), with the watchdog alleging the supermarket misled shoppers with effectively fake discounts on its “Prices Dropped” campaign.
after newsletter promotion
Prices unfrozen
During its price freeze period, Woolworths increased the retail price of 350g packs of RSPCA-approved chicken breast fillets by 33%.
While a customer would have paid $9 for the chicken breast fillets on 29 April, the price increased to $12 on 5 May. It then alternated between $9 and $12 twice more during the “Price Freeze”.
But, after the promotional period ended, the price dropped to $4.20 on 17 August.

Before the promotion, Woolworths’ 2kg bags of washed potatoes had consistently followed a routine high-low pricing pattern alternating between $6 and $8. This appears to have occurred during the promotional period, with CW Scanner data showing they cost customers $6 on 29 April, before the price went up to $8 on 6 May.
The price of a 12-pack of the supermarket’s own-brand fresh cinnamon donuts was increased from $3 to $3.50 on 6 May. It was reduced to $3 again on 18 August.
Choice’s senior campaigns and policy adviser, Bea Sherwood, said the advocacy group regularly heard from consumers who said they were confused by the pricing tickets they saw on supermarket shelves.

“Prices have changed so much over recent years and we’re seeing them continuously increase, so having an understanding of what a regular shelf price is is not something we can expect consumers to stay on top of,” Sherwood said.
“When Woolworths or Coles say something is a standard price, we don’t have the transparency to understand how they’ve come to that.”

articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine is a relentlessly bloody game with a sincere soap opera at its heart
articles.summary: The latest from Insomniac Games for the PlayStation 5 is a relentlessly paced action game that eschews an open world for constant forward momentum — and may initially shock players with its…

image.caption: The X-Men Wolverine (voice and performance capture by Liam McIntyre) and Jean Grey (Krizia Bajos) in Marvel's Wolverine, the new video game for the PlayStation 5. (Insomniac Games/Sony Interactive Entertainment)

blocks.text: You can't fault Sony for continuing to expand its video game-specific take on the Marvel Universe.

Its Marvel's Spider-Man games for the PlayStation consoles, by veteran in-house studio Insomniac Games, have been some of the platform's best-selling and reviewed games and indeed some of the most successful open-world games over the past decade.
Now, they're following up with Marvel's Wolverine, a more grizzled take on their original continuity starring the Canadian(ish) antihero James Logan Howlett.

The result is a relentlessly paced action game that eschews an open world for constant forward momentum — and may initially shock players with the bloodiest combat seen in a modern comic book adaptation other than Ryan Reynolds's R-rated Deadpool films.
A linear story with a rapid pace
Marvel's Wolverine nominally takes place in the same world as Insomniac's Spider-Man games, but you won't see any shocking crossovers here — appropriate, as we're telling a very different story.

The X-Men as we know them don't exist in this story; instead, we join the grumpy mutant with metal claws and a healing ability as part of Team X, a small commando group also including shapeshifter Mystique and Sabretooth (like Logan but bigger and angrier) under the mentorship of Nathaniel Essex, who instantly gives off vibes of a more sinister analog to Professor X.

You'll run into antagonists like Bolivar Trask, the scientist behind the mutant-hunting Sentinel robots, and Lady Deathstrike — Logan's sometimes-girlfriend, sometimes rival — here leading the Hand order of ninjas.

Instead of Spider-Man's open-world facsimile of Manhattan, Wolverine takes you more or less in a straight line through multiple locations including Tokyo and Marvel's fictional Southeast Asian nightlife town of Madripoor.

It will take most players roughly 12 to 15 hours to complete, whereas players could feasibly stretch the Spider-Man games to nearly double that. This game feels more like a globetrotting action film, or a comic book miniseries with a new location or villain subplot for each chapter.
It's bloody … very bloody
Unlike the Spider-Man games' teen-rated combat, Wolverine uses his claws to full effect, earning the game's Mature rating and then some.
With just a few button presses, Logan eviscerates, dismembers and impales humanoid enemies with breathtaking speed and savagery, fountains of blood splattering the landscape and his uniform alike.

Combat is fluid and mostly intuitive to the player, with most attacks mapped to the square and triangle face buttons; combining the controller's triggers and other buttons activates powered-up moves like spinning Logan's claws in a cyclone, or launching himself like a flying drill.

Most important is maintaining momentum; by continuously leaping at enemies and parrying incoming attacks you'll build up a rage meter that increases your damage and unlocks critical strikes that dispatch most low-level goons in one hit. Slow down your approach and you'll lose most of the bonuses, making things harder in the long run.

You'll break up the fighting with quieter moments like exploring Team X's headquarters or mingling with mutants at the Princess bar in Madripoor, but don't expect complex multilayered espionage like in the recent 007 First Light. They're mostly just there to give you a breather before you're thrown into yet another wave of enemies to eviscerate.
This is a Jean Grey story, too
Anyone familiar with Wolverine's lore across the screen and pages will know that he's often caught in a love triangle with fellow X-Men Cyclops and Jean Grey.
Jean, the uber-powerful user of telepathy and telekinesis, is the most important supporting character of this saga, while Cyclops is completely absent.
That makes way for a love story with more complexity than usual between Logan and Jean that slowly becomes the centrepiece of the game's narrative.

Jean will also accompany Logan through much of the back half of the game, levitating rubble to make traversable paths or aiding the player in combat by trapping enemies in place for you to attack, for example.
Canada in the (brief) spotlight

Most versions of Wolverine are nominally Canadian, having been born in Alberta and serving as part of the country's secret Weapon X program and crossing paths with Alpha Flight — the Canadian equivalent to the Avengers.

None of that history is relevant here, but we do spend some time in the Canadian North, where Team X's secret headquarters is based. You'll also take a walk in the snow before downing some off-brand Canadian rye whisky in Logan's log cabin, and first meet Jean in Vancouver before leaping into a motorcycle chase sequence along the Sea-to-Sky Highway.
Insomniac's art directors went to great lengths to make sure the landscape was accurately portrayed, including the Sḵwx̱wú7mesh sníchim (Squamish language) on highway signs.
The action moves so fast and furiously in this sequence, though, that you likely won't notice them as you leap from truck to truck and fling enemies to their deaths.
Marvel's Wolverine video game features Squamish Nation's language | Hanomansing Tonight
A narrative that outpaces the gameplay
Insomniac's Spider-Man games stood out for their stories that remixed well-known characters' origins in a way that can surprise even the most well-read comic book fan, and Wolverine is no different.
(While review spoiler guidelines prevent a full account of the story, it does some novel things with Jean's background that X-Men fans will either find intriguing or infuriating.)

It's easy to get sucked into the game's final chapters and narrative crescendo — to the point that when the non-interactable cutscenes end and you're thrown back into control, it can feel like an obligation or a chore.
It doesn't help that some boss fights, while visually spectacular, aren't mechanically different enough from other fights; they just take longer to pummel into submission.
It's a credit to Insomniac's visuals and direction team that I found myself thinking about the actors' performances as much as I have for any other narrative-heavy game.

Most of the main characters' faces are based at least somewhat on their performance actors' real-life likenesses. They're animated with impressive realism — Liam McIntyre's Wolverine in particular emotes with convincing rage and puppy-dog empathy alike, especially opposite Krizia Bajos's Jean Grey.
They impart a whiff of the uncanny valley, though, as the rest of the world feels ripped from the more stylized pages of a modern comic book.

Despite the shorter run time and narrower scope, Insomniac did not water down the experience for its first X-Men foray. Indeed, Marvel's Wolverine might be the purest distillation of the character's gnarliest comic book appearances — heavy on the uncensored violence but also the yearning soap opera at the core of many X-stories.
If you have a PlayStation 5 — and the stomach for a bloodier outing than most — it's not one to miss.
Marvel's Wolverine is available exclusively for Sony's PlayStation 5 and PlayStation 5 Pro on Sept. 15.

articles.title: North Korea spends war windfall on arms, infrastructure
articles.summary: The Ukraine war and Pyongyang's alliance with Moscow have delivered an economic boost to North Korea, allowing the regime to pursue a range of long-desired projects.

image.caption: On Tuesday, North Korea and Russia opened their first road bridge across the Tumen River, with customs posts and warehousing facilities under construction on both sides of the waterwayImage: Yuri Smityuk/TASS/picture alliance

blocks.text: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un is spending the money that his troops have earned fighting in Ukraine to fund a long wish list of projects that were previously beyond his financial reach.

South Korea's National Intelligence Service estimated in May that Pyongyang received a minimum of $7.7 billion (€6.6 billion) in financial aid and economic value from Russia in the preceding three years for committing men and materiel to Moscow's war against Ukraine — and potentially as much as $14 billion.
That is a significant amount given that the North's GDP for 2024 stood at $26.6 billion.
Kim's support for Russia has been lucrative, and a slew of reports are now identifying where that money is being spent.

A portion of the funds is being put aside for the Regional Development 20x10 Policy, unveiled in January 2024 and which aims to construct modern industrial facilities in 20 regional cities per year for the next 10 years to improve living standards outside Pyongyang.
Why a new Russia-North Korea road bridge worries Ukraine
Benefiting from Russian money
More civil programs are being designed, observers say, although most appear to be earmarked for the "elites" who reside in Pyongyang.

"Before the alliance with Russia, the general infrastructure was poor due to a mixture of economic mismanagement and sanctions," said Martyn Williams, senior fellow for the Korea program at the Stimson Center in Washington DC.
"With the breakdown in consensus on the United Nations Security Council and renewed trade with China and Russia, things are starting to move along now," he told DW.

"There are several large programs to build factories and hospitals across the country, [Kim] has ordered the development of entire new districts of Pyongyang and there's a rural housing project building tens of thousands of rural homes," he said, along with investment in "the modernization of several sectors of the economy."
There are, however, structural problems that still need to be overcome, he said.

"There is investment going into building, but the large new hospital in central Pyongyang was built some time ago and sat unused for a while, until medicines and equipment could be procured," he said. "North Korea is great at building, but keeping it running is the key — so we look to see if that will happen."
South Korea proposes talks to officially end war with North
IAEA warns of new nuclear facility

More of the financial windfall is clearly being put into the military. On Wednesday, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said it had identified a new uranium enrichment facility at the Yongbyon Nuclear Complex with an estimated 28 cascades of centrifuges.
The IAEA estimated that the facility would permit the regime to produce 85 kilograms of weapons-grade highly enriched uranium a year, enough for four nuclear warheads.
Satellite images also show that the North is enlarging and upgrading the west coast port of Nampo and Chongjin, on the east coast of the peninsula, to accommodate a new generation of warships.

On Monday, Kim attended the commissioning ceremony in Wonsan of the 5,000-ton destroyer Kang Kon, with the North Korean leader claiming the vessel was capable of launching nuclear weapons and would be able to "deal a deadly retaliatory blow at the enemies."

The third area of heavy investment has been in major improvements in roads, ports and bridges. This is infrastructure that stagnated during years of isolation under international sanctions but is today required to facilitate the deployment of more troops to Russia and the arrival of advanced military technology, energy and consumer goods in return.

On Tuesday, North Korea and Russia opened their first road bridge across the Tumen River, with customs posts and warehousing facilities under construction on both sides of the waterway. The bridge underlines the rapidly expanding ties since Kim and President Vladimir Putin announced a comprehensive strategic partnership in 2024.

The route will permit greater truck-borne exchanges, reduce costs and potentially be used for the transit of North Korean men, weapons and ammunition to Russia. It also further reduces the leverage of sanctions on North Korea.
North Korea expands role in Russia's war with Ukraine

"A lot of these projects, such as improving trans-border rail and road connections, building customs facilities and so on, were started before the pandemic and have followed an on-again-off-again pattern ever since," said Marcus Noland, executive vice president at the Peterson Institute for International Economics in Washington.

"After difficult times during the pandemic, which was accompanied by border closure, the North Korean economy appears to have grown for the last several years on the back of Ukraine war revenues and cybercrime."
Hinterland 'stagnating'

Noland said he has the impression that Pyongyang is faring relatively well economically, along with a number of cities on the China border thanks to renewed trade, "but the hinterland continues to stagnate."
While the Ukraine conflict and Pyongyang's alliance with Moscow have been an economic boon to North Korea, analysts say, it's not clear what will happen when the war inevitably comes to an end.

"The North Korean regime could be in a difficult spot if peace were to break out in Ukraine," said Noland. "If the war-related revenues were to dry up, the country could experience an economic decline and associated discontent after a period of rising expectations," he stressed.
"I am not saying that it would be enough to destabilize the system, but I do think that a transition to peace in Ukraine could present challenges that would have to be navigated by the regime."

articles.title: Jodi Sta. Maria joins cast of ‘2nd Miracle in Cell No. 7’
articles.summary: Jodi Sta. Maria is joining Aga Muhlach and Xia Vigor in “2nd Miracle in Cell No. 7,” the sequel to the hit 2019 Philippine adaptation of the Korean drama film “Miracle in Cell No. 7.” Viva Films…

blocks.text: Jodi Sta. Maria is joining Aga Muhlach and Xia Vigor in “2nd Miracle in Cell No. 7,” the sequel to the hit 2019 Philippine adaptation of the Korean drama film “Miracle in Cell No. 7.”

Viva Films announced Sta. Maria’s casting on Thursday, Sept. 10, on social media. She will play a character named Angela in the upcoming film, which is set to be part of the 2026 Metro Manila Film Festival (MMFF).

The announcement unites Sta. Maria with Muhlach and Vigor, who are reprising their respective roles as Joselito “Lito” Gopez and Yesha Gopez from the first film. The sequel is directed by Nuel Crisostomo Naval, who also helmed the 2019 adaptation.
Viva Films has yet to disclose the complete plot of “2nd Miracle in Cell No. 7,” including how Angela figures into the story.

The original “Miracle in Cell No. 7” was a 2013 South Korean comedy-drama directed by Lee Hwan-kyung. It follows Yong-gu, a man with an intellectual disability who is wrongfully imprisoned for the death of a young girl.
Inside prison, Yong-gu develops a friendship with his fellow inmates, who eventually help him secretly reunite with his young daughter, Ye-sung.

The story later follows Ye-sung as an adult lawyer who seeks to prove her father’s innocence. The Korean film became a major box-office success, surpassing 10 million admissions in South Korea and eventually exceeding 12 million viewers.
View this post on Instagram A post shared by VIVA Films (@viva_films)

The Philippine version was released as an official entry to the 2019 Metro Manila Film Festival (MMFF). The film starred Muhlach, Vigor and Bela Padilla, who played adult Yesha. Its supporting cast included Joel Torre, John Arcilla, JC Santos, Mon Confiado, Soliman Cruz and Tirso Cruz III.
“Miracle in Cell No. 7” became one of the biggest films of the 2019 MMFF and was eventually reported to have earned P475 million at the Philippine box office, according to producer Viva Films.
Meanwhile, Sta. Maria recently starred in the films “Midnight Girls,” “Ganito, Ganyan, Ganoon,” and “Edjop.”

articles.title: Florida man scheduled for execution in connection to Hog Trail Murders
articles.summary:
Daniel Owen Conahan Jr’s sentence will make him the state’s 15th person executed this year

A Florida man was scheduled for execution on Thursday after being convicted of one of a series of…

blocks.text: A Florida man was scheduled for execution on Thursday after being convicted of one of a series of suspected killings that became known as the Hog Trail Murders in the 1990s.

Daniel Owen Conahan Jr, 72, was sentenced to die by lethal injection for the 1996 kidnapping and strangling of Richard Allen Montgomery. Authorities found Montgomery’s mutilated body in a wooded south-west Florida area where the remains of at least six people have been found over a three-year span.

Florida has carried out more than half of the 24 total executions in the US this year, under Ron DeSantis, the Republican governor who leaves office in January. Conahan Jr’s sentence will make him the state’s 15th person executed this year.
Under DeSantis, Florida carried out 19 executions in 2025, setting a state record since the death penalty was reinstated in 1976.

Conahan was arrested in July 1996 after local and state law enforcement officials spent more than two years investigating a series of homicides in which mutilated and decomposing bodies were discovered in a wooded area of Charlotte county, north of Fort Myers.

The deaths eventually were categorized as the Hog Trail Murders because of the swampy, wooded locations where the bodies were found. The case has been featured many times over the past three decades on true-crime media content.

Conahan, who has maintained his innocence, was previously identified by authorities as a person of interest in the other deaths, but he was never charged. He argued that the evidence against him was circumstantial.

The first body was found by hunters in February 1994, followed by at least five more bodies over the next three years. Most of the remains were severely decomposed, but investigators believed Montgomery had been dead for less than a day when he was found.
Investigators eventually determined that the killer was targeting men who were unhoused.

Detectives started looking into Conahan in 1996 after a man in prison for stealing Conahan’s car claimed that Conahan had lured him to a remote area and offered to pay him to pose for nude photos. The man said he drove off in the car after seeing a knife.
Conahan waived his right to a jury trial and was convicted by a judge of murder and kidnapping in August 1999.
The Florida supreme court last week denied Conahan’s final appeals, including one requesting additional testing on DNA collected from the victim.

The petition said he has been requesting DNA testing since March 2025 of evidence collected at the scene and from Montgomery’s body to “conclusively establish that he is not responsible for the death”.
Within 24 hours, the court ruled that proving Montgomery had DNA on his body from someone other than Conahan wouldn’t exonerate him.
A final appeal remains pending before the US supreme court.

articles.title: Trump’s promise of $5,000 ‘dividend’ for US citizens after midterms met with incredulity
articles.summary:
Critics call bid for Republican votes ‘bribery’ and point to potential $1.2tn cost added to existing national debt

Donald Trump’s promise of a $5,000 “Trump dividend” for every US citizen if…

blocks.text: Donald Trump’s promise of a $5,000 “Trump dividend” for every US citizen if Republicans retain control of the US Congress in November’s midterm elections has sparked incredulity and accusations of bribery.
“If the Republicans win, you win with us and you get $5,000,” Trump said during the unprecedented Republican midterm convention in Dallas. “It will be called the Trump dividend.”
It comes amid extreme concern over the US national debt, which exceeded $40tn for the first time in August.

Speaking to Politico, Chip Roy, the Republican US representative from Texas, sounded skeptical. “Well – I would like to know how they would plan to pay for … back of envelope … well over $1tn,” he said.

In the moments after Trump made the announcement, Marc Goldwein of the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget wrote on X that “this would cost about $1.2 TRILLION in just one year. That’s more than ALL THREE ROUNDS of COVID relief checks, despite no recessions. The result would be a huge spike in the deficit, and almost certainly in the inflation rate.”
The US has roughly 240 million adult citizens, suggesting the cost of $1.2tn. The federal government spent about $7tn in fiscal year 2025, with about $2tn taken on as debt.
Democratic political leaders reacted with blunt condemnation.

“After making you sicker and poorer with his war, Donald Trump now wants to buy your vote with $5,000 in taxpayer-funded blood money,” the California governor Gavin Newsom said. “The most corrupt man ever to occupy the Oval Office.”

The Democratic National Committee (DNC) pointed to Trump’s record on similar pledges, from $5,000 stimulus checks as a result of the work of the so-called department of government efficiency (Doge) to $2,000 stimulus checks from revenue from tariffs.

“Donald Trump and Republicans are once again offering empty promises to Americans,” said Kendall Witmer, the committee’s rapid response director. “The only people reaping the benefits of Trump’s economy are himself, his family, and his ultra-rich elite donors. Meanwhile, working families get nothing except sky-high receipts at the grocery store and the pump, unaffordable healthcare premiums, and wages that aren’t keeping up with inflation.”

The Bipartisan Policy Center has been tracking tariff revenue since Trump began raising rates in 2025. As of 8 September, the US has collected about $210bn in tariff and excise tax revenue in 2026. At a rate of $21bn per month, the US federal government would have to collect tariffs for nearly five years to cover a $5,000 payment, assuming every dollar of tariff revenue went to the payment, and discounting tariff payments refunded to retailers in legal challenges.
Peter Schiff, chief economist for Euro Pacific Asset Management, said that Trump’s pledge had already begun rippling through financial markets.

“Even though bond investors know that, even in the unlikely event Republicans retain control of the House, Trump’s promise to borrow over $1 trillion more to buy votes won’t be kept,” Schiff wrote in a post on X. “The promise itself is so reckless that they’re dumping Treasuries, sending yields to new highs …

“Making his promise even worse, Trump referred to his $5,000 bribes as ‘dividends’, as if his policies had been so successful that the US now has surpluses to share. Instead, his reckless policies have produced massive deficits. Trump needs to send Americans bills, not checks.”
JD Vance appeared to walk back Trump’s pledge, suggesting that the benefit would be means-tested.

But the US senator Bernie Moreno, an Ohio Republican, promised support for Trump’s idea. “I will get a bill ready so that we can get the Trump Dividend passed immediately after the November 3rd election,” Moreno wrote on X.

articles.title: NHS reports busiest ever summer as heatwaves drive up hospital admissions
articles.summary:
Record demand for A&E units, ambulance services and NHS 111 shows extreme heat having unprecedented impact on health, experts say

The NHS came under its most intense strain ever as a…

blocks.text: The NHS came under its most intense strain ever as a result of the summer’s five heatwaves, amid warnings that extreme heat is having an unprecedented impact on human health.
A&E units, ambulance services and the NHS 111 telephone advice line all experienced record demand for their services in England in June, July and August as Britain experienced record temperatures.

NHS England’s latest performance statistics, published on Thursday, prompted claims that the growing climate emergency has left the NHS with a “twin crisis” as it struggles to meet patients’ need for care in the summer as well as winter.
“Extreme heat is now an NHS pressure point, not just a weather story,” said Sarah Woolnough, the chief executive of the King’s Fund health thinktank.
“The NHS is now facing a twin crisis with summer joining winter as a major pressure on services and leaving little room for staff and the system to recover between peak periods.

“One major factor is climate change. As its effects become more pronounced and record-breaking heatwaves become more frequent, the impacts on people’s health and our health system are becoming more obvious,” she added.

Almost 7.3 million people attended A&E units in England in June, July and August – the highest number ever seen in the summer. The total of 7,268,445 attendances was 240,000 more than the 7,027,384 who attended in the same months in 2025, NHS England said.
Almost a million more people sought help at A&E this summer than in the same period in 2022.

It was a similar picture with other key NHS services. There was also a record number of ambulance callouts this summer – 2.46m, up from 2.32m in the same period last year. And NHS 111 answered just over 3m calls over the summer months – more than 100,000 up year-on-year.

“Despite a scorching summer which has tested the NHS like never before and seen demand rocket to record levels, staff have risen magnificently to the challenge to deliver for patients”, said Prof Frankie Swords, NHS England’s national medical director.

Yvette Cooper, the health secretary, acknowledged the new challenge that very high temperatures were posing for the NHS, when she said that “the reality is that extreme demand is no longer confined to winter”.

She announced that £1.5bn of NHS funding would be used to give hospitals extra capacity through the construction of new operating theatres, children’s wards and improved maternitynunits, as well as measures to “heat-proof” the NHS. However, the latter was only allocated £32m of the £1.5bn, the Department of Health and Social Care said.
after newsletter promotion
The DHSC has set up a heat taskforce to come up with ideas to help the NHS cope with extreme heat. Many hospitals struggled to maintain normal care this summer during the heatwaves.

“August was the world’s joint hottest month on record and the health impact is clear to see in hospitals across the country,” said Andrew McCracken, the director of external affairs at the charity Asthma + Lung UK.
“Breathing issues are already the leading cause of emergency admissions in England and it’s likely that this summer increase is in part being driven by respiratory problems.

“As temperatures rise it becomes harder to breathe. Layer on top smoke from wildfires, pollution trapped by the high pressure and a longer pollen season and people with lung conditions like asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease are facing a barrage of potential triggers,” he added.
In worrying news for the government Thursday’s figures also showed that the NHS waiting list in England for hospital rose in July to 7.3 million – the highest figure since last October.
The rise raises doubts about the likelihood of the government meeting its pledge to ensure the NHS is once again treating 92% of people on the waiting list within 18 weeks by 2029.

articles.title: France’s Epstein probe identifies ‘potential recruiters’
articles.summary: PARIS, France — A French investigation into alleged human trafficking that enabled US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein to commit abuses is pursuing several leads on potential recruiters, a prosecutor…

blocks.text: PARIS, France — A French investigation into alleged human trafficking that enabled US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein to commit abuses is pursuing several leads on potential recruiters, a prosecutor said Thursday.
Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau spoke after French modeling scout Daniel Siad, who is accused of helping Epstein traffic women, was found dead at his home in July before he could be questioned.
“We have obtained other names of potential recruiters,” she told France Inter radio.
“For us, the Epstein network is a labyrinthine network. To get out of it, it’s not just a single Ariadne’s thread you have to pull on, it’s dozens and dozens of threads,” she said.
The investigation has so far led authorities to New York and “towards Saint-Tropez, towards Cannes,” she added.

France opened a human trafficking investigation after the US Justice Department in January released the latest cache of files from its investigation into the disgraced financier, who died in prison in 2019 while facing charges of trafficking underage girls for sex.
Beccuau said 26 victims had been identified, including eight who still needed to be questioned because some lived abroad.
“Of these 26 victims, 13 had not previously appeared in any case,” she said.
French authorities have previously looked into other figures in the French modeling industry.

Magistrates previously dropped an investigation into sexual assault and rape allegations against Gerald Marie, the former European head of the Elite modeling agency who is now in his mid-70s, because the alleged abuse was beyond the statute of limitations.
Several women have urged new investigations targeting him since the release of the latest Epstein files.
Marie last month denied any wrongdoing, telling RTL: “I have never raped anyone.”
“I’ve always behaved consistently and properly with women. I love women. I can’t see myself forcing one,” he added.
He said he met Epstein only once.
French police in 2020 also arrested modeling agent Jean-Luc Brunel after allegations that he procured women for the US billionaire. He was found dead in prison in 2022.
